answer: A skill I would really love to learn is public speaking, something I have always found rather [[daunting]]. I can talk comfortably to one student at a time, but standing in front of a room full of people is a completely different story. I want to learn it because being able to speak confidently in front of others is genuinely valuable, both professionally and personally. At the moment, the thought of addressing a large audience makes me quite nervous, and I would love to overcome that. In fact, my consultancy sometimes holds information sessions for students and parents, and I usually let my colleagues do the talking. I would probably start by joining a speaking club, where I could practise regularly in a supportive environment. There are a few groups like that in Dhaka, and some even meet online, which would suit someone living outside the capital like me. I might also record myself and watch it back, which sounds painful but would show me exactly what to improve. I know it would require stepping well outside my comfort zone and a good deal of [[perseverance]]. Still, I believe the reward would be immense. Being an effective communicator could open up all sorts of opportunities in my career, and it would make me far more [[articulate]] in meetings. Honestly, I think it is one of the most [[empowering]] skills a person can develop. It would also boost my confidence in everyday situations. It is definitely near the top of my list of things to work on once I have the time to commit to it properly.

followUps.q: Have you ever had to give a speech?
followUps.answer: Yes, once at my university farewell programme. I had to say a few words on behalf of my batch, and although my hands were shaking, everyone was kind, and I felt quite proud afterwards.

followUps.q: Do you think public speaking can be taught?
followUps.answer: I think so. Some people are naturally confident, but most good speakers have simply practised a lot. With honest feedback and regular practice, even a fairly [[reserved]] person can become comfortable in front of an audience.

note: Unmarked plain 'nervous'; added consultancy information sessions, a second learning method and [[articulate]]; tied to his job.
